feedback.problem:
Construct the matrix of the linear transformation that acts on a vector in ${R}^{2}$ as follows (in the order given):

- it rotates the vector by $\frac{3\pi }{2}$ radians counterclockwise about the origin, and then

- applies a shear transformation to the result with a shear factor of $3$ parallel to the $x$-axis.
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $P$ be the matrix that represents the rotation and let $Q$ be the matrix that represents the shear. These are given by the following elementary transformation matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\ Q & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the combined transformation can be represented by the matrix $QP:$

$$
\begin{aligned}QP & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
